name: Live simulation trace (gauge, log and chart on one clock)

source.description: 1 inspected reference film (batch-6, 2026-11-26): a square explainer runs a rate limiter live for 18 s: a gauge, an event log and a chart driven by one clock, with a one-line regime caption.

technique: A system is explained by running it. One deterministic event script drives a state gauge (a big count and a bar stack), a scrolling event log and a time-series chart, all advanced by one clock, so the three views always agree. A one-line caption at the top names the current regime and swaps in place when the regime changes; there are no transitions.
purpose: Explain a system by running it: three views of one state always agree, and the regime caption tells the viewer what to watch.
visual_behaviour: A big count with a bar stack, a scrolling event log and a step chart advance together on one stage; a one-line caption at the top names the current regime and swaps in place; there are no transitions; the final state holds for several seconds.
mechanics: One timeline clock; an event list [{t, kind}] from a seeded script. Each event updates the gauge (count and bar stack; the count turns red at 0), appends a log row (time, id, outcome in green or red, remainder) and adds a tick on the chart axis while the chart line steps to the new value. Measured: a burst drains 9 -> 0 between 2.50 and 3.36 s (one event per 0.07-0.1 s); single refills flicker 0 -> 1 -> 0 at the refill period (4.31-5.41 s); recovery 2 -> 10 over about 4.5 s. Regime caption: one line of 5-9 words swapped in place 4 times in 18 s; the closing rule in an accent colour; hold the final state 3-6 s.

decomposition.timing: Regimes of 0.8-5.9 s; the burst is the shortest, the closing rule the longest.

parameters.name: burstRate
parameters.description: Events per second during the burst

parameters.name: capacity
parameters.description: Maximum state value shown by the gauge

parameters.name: logRows
parameters.description: Visible rows in the event log

use_cases: Rate limiters, queues, caches, retries, backpressure
Any algorithm whose state evolves over time (proof-canvas, systems-blueprint templates)
failure_modes: Views that disagree by one event destroy trust: drive all three from one event list
More than about 10 events per second become unreadable: aggregate or slow the clock
Without the regime caption the viewer does not know what to watch

implementation.approach: Studio.comp.simulation(parent, {capacity, events, regimes, duration}) with Studio.comp.simulationScript(seed, phases) (runtime 1.18.0): the state after every event is precomputed once; one proxy clock picks the event index and redraws the gauge count (red at 0) and cells, the last log rows (outcome colour on a marker dot, text in ink for contrast), the clip over the step chart and its ticks, and the regime caption (0.15 s fade in place).

requirements: chart and counter updates per event

provenance.observed: A token bucket of 10 simulated live for 18 s on one square stage: count, bar stack, a six-row request log and a step chart advance together; 9 -> 0 between 2.50 and 3.36 s during the burst; a regime line swaps in place four times; the final state holds 5.9 s.
